checks: The frozen formulas match e8b3121d2cddc568 §2, (4)–(6). The statement assumes the original row probability, its mean, common plane and positive finite weights, so no unproved surface coupling is needed.

Subtracting the plane equality at w gives n·(X′−X)=−a·(z′−z), hence the exact weight increment with both minus signs. The unweighted row has mean-zero increments, eliminating the a term from the scalar mass difference and the constant r(w) from the vector defect.

Affine centers make the weight increment a linear form with coefficient −(a+Aᵀn,0). Its mean is zero. The vector defect is −Q times that coefficient without its minus sign, and Q is positive semidefinite. Its vanishing is equivalent to zero variance of the weight increment and hence constancy almost surely.
The normalized target barycenter equals w exactly when the unnormalized vector defect is zero. Strict positivity of the weights ensures a positive normalization, including the degenerate row case.

overlap.comparison: Its compact convex-order result can produce the unweighted mean-preserving rows; it gives no condition for target reweighting to preserve them.
Its anchored affine support slopes can supply a common support-plane label, but do not evaluate the covariance correction induced by cone weights.

summary: The mass and vector defects follow from the same support-plane equality, and the affine-center case gives exactly the covariance condition for preserving the row barycenter.
